Attachment

Built from parts

Section titled “Built from parts”

An attachment is <sl:attachment> plus the parts you need: <sl:attachment-media> (an icon or an image), <sl:attachment-content> (holding <sl:attachment-title> and <sl:attachment-description>), <sl:attachment-actions> with one or more <sl:attachment-action>s, and an optional <sl:attachment-trigger> that makes the whole card clickable. <sl:attachment-group> lays several out in a row or a grid.

The attachment only shows a file; it uploads nothing. Use it for files that are already on the server, such as the documents on a customer’s page, and for the list of a file upload, where your page or your script sets each one’s state.

An <sl:attachment-action> is an <sl:button>, ghost and an extra small icon by default. It holds only an icon, so give it an aria-label that names the file: “Remove report.pdf”, not just “Remove”, because a page can show many.

A title or description that does not fit is cut off with an ellipsis. Without full-width an attachment is as wide as its content; with it, it fills its container, for a list of attachments.

Image

Section titled “Image”

<sl:attachment-media variant="image"> crops an <img> to fill the media’s square. orientation="vertical" puts the media above the content. The title already names the file, so the image can have an empty alt.

The image is your own <img>, so it works under a strict Content Security Policy as long as it comes from your own server: point th:src at a thumbnail URL, such as @{/files/{id}/thumbnail(id=${file.id})}. A data: URL would need data: in img-src, which a strict policy leaves out.

States

Section titled “States”

state says where a file is in its upload:

  • idle: picked, not sent yet. A dashed border.
  • uploading and processing: the title shimmers (not for users who ask for reduced motion) and an image is dimmed. The attachment is marked busy (aria-busy="true").
  • error: a destructive border, media and description.
  • done, the default: the file is there.

The state is not announced by itself. Say it in the description as well (“Uploading · 64%”, “Upload failed. Try again.”), so it is not told by colour alone and a screen reader reads it with the file. The attachment is no live region and has no role="alert": a page that renders a failed upload would announce it on every load. When a script changes the state, it should announce the change itself, once, in one polite live region for the whole list.

An <sl:spinner> in the media shows that a file is uploading. The description already says so: give the spinner aria-hidden="true", so “Loading” is not read too. There is no progress bar; show the percentage in the description.

Sizes

Section titled “Sizes”

size is default, sm or xs.

Group

Section titled “Group”

<sl:attachment-group> lays attachments out in a row that scrolls sideways when they do not fit, snapping to each attachment, its edges fading out. The scrollbar is hidden: the fade shows there is more.

Keyboard users reach attachments off screen by tabbing to their actions or triggers. A row of attachments without any has nothing to tab to: give the group a label. It is then a named group (role="group") that takes the focus, and the arrow keys scroll it.

Grid

Section titled “Grid”

layout="grid" wraps the attachments instead, in as many columns as fit the width, for a gallery of photos. It does not scroll, so nothing is hidden off screen and the edges do not fade. Give each attachment orientation="vertical" and full-width, so it fills its cell: the image is cropped to a square and the actions sit in its corner. The width of a cell and the gap between them come from the skin.

A grid’s label still makes it a named group, but the group takes no focus: there is nothing to scroll. Tab goes from one attachment’s actions and trigger to the next.

Trigger

Section titled “Trigger”

<sl:attachment-trigger> covers the whole card, behind its actions, so a click anywhere but on an action activates it. It is a button, to open an <sl:dialog> with commandfor and command="show-modal", or with as="a" a link that opens the file. It has no text of its own: give it an aria-label that says what it does. Put it last in the attachment, so Tab reaches the actions first; its focus ring is drawn around the whole card.

Download

Section titled “Download”

An action can be a link (as="a") and take any of the button’s variants and sizes, such as a download button in a message thread.

On a page with hx-boost, add hx-boost="false" to a download link: htmx boosts every link to your own server without a target, download or not, and would put the file’s bytes into the page instead of saving it. A trigger that opens the file in a new tab (target="_blank") is left alone.

Without content

Section titled “Without content”

An attachment can be only its media, as an image in a chat message. Then the image’s alt names it.

Attributes

Section titled “Attributes”

sl:attachment

Section titled “sl:attachment”
AttributeValuesDefaultDescription
stateidle uploading processing error donedoneWhere the file is in its upload: idle (picked, not sent yet) draws a dashed border, uploading and processing shimmer the title and mark the attachment busy (aria-busy), error turns it destructive. done is a file that is there.
sizedefault sm xsdefaultSize of the attachment.
orientationhorizontal verticalhorizontalvertical puts the media above the content, for an image.
full-widthboolean—Fill the width of the container, for a list of attachments. Without it the attachment is as wide as its content.

Every prop can also be set from an expression: th:state="${...}". Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and class is appended.

sl:attachment-media

Section titled “sl:attachment-media”
AttributeValuesDefaultDescription
varianticon imageiconicon centres an icon on a muted square; image crops an &lt;img&gt; to fill the square, dimmed while the attachment uploads, is processed or failed.

Every prop can also be set from an expression: th:variant="${...}". Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and class is appended.

sl:attachment-content

Section titled “sl:attachment-content”

sl:attachment-content declares no props; every attribute passes through.

sl:attachment-title

Section titled “sl:attachment-title”

sl:attachment-title declares no props; every attribute passes through.

sl:attachment-description

Section titled “sl:attachment-description”

sl:attachment-description declares no props; every attribute passes through.

sl:attachment-actions

Section titled “sl:attachment-actions”

sl:attachment-actions declares no props; every attribute passes through.

sl:attachment-action

Section titled “sl:attachment-action”
AttributeValuesDefaultDescription
variantdefault outline ghost destructive secondary linkghostVisual style of the button, as on sl:button.
sizexs sm default lg icon icon-xs icon-sm icon-lgicon-xsSize of the button, as on sl:button. The icon sizes are square, for a button that holds only an icon, and need an aria-label.
asbutton abuttonElement to render: a button, or an anchor (a) to download or open the file.

Every prop can also be set from an expression: th:variant="${...}". Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and class is appended. An aria-label or aria-labelledby is required when size is icon, icon-xs, icon-sm or icon-lg; rendering fails without one.

sl:attachment-trigger

Section titled “sl:attachment-trigger”
AttributeValuesDefaultDescription
asbutton abuttonElement to render: a button, or an anchor (a) to open the file.

Every prop can also be set from an expression: th:as="${...}". Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and class is appended. An aria-label or aria-labelledby is required; rendering fails without one.

sl:attachment-group

Section titled “sl:attachment-group”
AttributeValuesDefaultDescription
layoutrow gridrowrow scrolls sideways; grid wraps the attachments in columns that fill the width, for a gallery of photos: vertical attachments with full-width, each filling its cell.
labelstring—Accessible name of the group. With it the group is a named group (role="group"). A row then takes keyboard focus, so the arrow keys scroll it: for a row of attachments that have no actions or trigger. A grid does not scroll, so it takes no focus.

Every prop can also be set from an expression: th:layout="${...}". Any other attribute passes through to the rendered element, and class is appended.
